detections.evidence_quote: So the way I really think about longevity in blood is the three things that you're looking for in blood disease-wise are
detections.summary: Host asks whether blood tests can predict lifespan; guest frames longevity blood work as assessing risk of atherosclerotic disease, cancer and neurodegeneration.

detections.evidence_quote: what you're not going to get on a standard blood test is any of the longevity genes
detections.summary: Guest notes standard blood tests do not show longevity genes, naming APOE as one.

detections.evidence_quote: So the lower your LP little A, the greater your chance of cardiovascular mortality.
detections.summary: Guest calls Lp(a) an inverse longevity gene and links its level to cardiovascular mortality.

detections.evidence_quote: so heart disease or stroke? What is this person's risk of cancer? What is this person's risk of neurodegenerative disease?
detections.summary: Guest lists stroke, cancer and neurodegenerative disease risk as what longevity blood work looks for.

detections.evidence_quote: Cardiovascular disease largely driven by three things: lipoproteins, inflammation, endothelial dysfunction.
detections.summary: Guest explains assessing atherosclerotic heart disease risk via lipoproteins, inflammation and endothelial markers in blood, plus CT angiograms and calcium scores.

detections.evidence_quote: On the lipoprotein side, we can see most of what we want, which is the Lp little a, the LDL, the small LDL.
detections.summary: Guest says blood tests reveal most lipoprotein information: Lp(a), LDL and small LDL particle number, and VLDL.

detections.evidence_quote: On the inflammation side, we can see specific and non-specific markers of inflammation.
detections.summary: Guest lists non-specific (fibrinogen, CRP) and specific (ox-LDL, Lp-PLA2) inflammation markers measurable in blood.

detections.evidence_quote: I include insulin here because I think that insulin is, in and of itself, actually toxic at high levels to the endothelium.
detections.summary: Guest includes insulin among endothelial markers, saying high insulin is toxic to the endothelium, citing a paper using insulin doses in type 1 diabetics.

detections.evidence_quote: looked at cardiovascular health in patients with type 1 diabetes
detections.summary: A paper on cardiovascular health in type 1 diabetes patients that used their insulin doses is mentioned.

detections.evidence_quote: The older a patient gets, the more I would probably rely on things like CT angiograms
detections.summary: Guest says older patients need CT angiograms and that calcium scores are of limited value since many events occur at non-calcified lesions.

detections.evidence_quote: until companies like GRAIL have fully functioning liquid biopsies, where you're looking at, I think GRAIL is probably looking mostly at RNA and DNA.
detections.summary: Guest says blood gives little insight into cancer risk until liquid biopsies such as GRAIL's are fully functioning.

detections.evidence_quote: virtually every cancer is a result of a somatic mutation, not a germline mutation.
detections.summary: Guest says most cancers arise from somatic mutations, so cancer risk comes down to inflammation and metabolic health.

detections.evidence_quote: So, knowing your genotype doesn't really help, outside of a few outlier things like BRCA or Lynch.
detections.summary: Guest says knowing one's genotype does little for cancer risk except for outliers like BRCA or Lynch.

detections.evidence_quote: in cancer, it really comes down to understanding inflammation, which we've already addressed, and metabolic health
detections.summary: Guest ties cancer risk to inflammation and metabolic health and stresses minimizing hyperinsulinemia.

detections.evidence_quote: insulin is, in and of itself, actually toxic at high levels to the endothelium
detections.summary: Insulin's toxicity to the endothelium is offered as the reason to count it as an endothelial-health marker.

detections.evidence_quote: James O'Keefe just recently was on a paper that looked at cardiovascular health in patients with type 1 diabetes
detections.summary: Guest cites a recent paper with James O'Keefe on cardiovascular health in type 1 diabetes patients using insulin doses.

detections.evidence_quote: an editorial that came out two days ago, based on a study in one of the atherosclerosis journals, was you know looking at fifty percent of patients that had that had events
detections.summary: Guest cites a recent editorial on a study in an atherosclerosis journal finding half of events occurred at non-calcified lesions.

detections.evidence_quote: virtually every cancer is a result of a somatic mutation, not a germline mutation. So, knowing your genotype doesn't really help
detections.summary: Somatic rather than germline origin of cancer is offered to explain why genotyping does not help predict cancer.

verification_candidates.claim_text: APOE is one of the longevity genes.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: you certainly APOE would be one of the longevity genes
verification_candidates.rationale: A claim about a gene's link to lifespan that genetic studies can check.

verification_candidates.claim_text: The lower a person's Lp(a), the greater their chance of cardiovascular mortality.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: So the lower your LP little A, the greater your chance of cardiovascular mortality.
verification_candidates.rationale: States the direction of the Lp(a)-mortality relationship, which epidemiology can confirm or contradict.

verification_candidates.claim_text: Cardiovascular disease is largely driven by three things: lipoproteins, inflammation and endothelial dysfunction.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: Cardiovascular disease largely driven by three things: lipoproteins, inflammation, endothelial dysfunction.
verification_candidates.rationale: A causal model of heart disease that shapes which risk factors listeners attend to.

verification_candidates.claim_text: Insulin is, in and of itself, toxic to the endothelium at high levels.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: I think that insulin is, in and of itself, actually toxic at high levels to the endothelium.
verification_candidates.rationale: A causal claim about hyperinsulinemia damaging blood vessels that research can test.

verification_candidates.claim_text: Asymmetric dimethylarginine (ADMA) and SDMA are inhibitors of nitric oxide synthase.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: asymmetric dimethylarginine, or ADMA, and SDMA, which are inhibitors of nitric oxide synthase
verification_candidates.rationale: A biochemical mechanism offered to justify an endothelial blood marker.

verification_candidates.claim_text: For a 40-year-old without dramatic abnormalities, blood tests probably reveal eighty to eighty-five percent of what is needed to know about cardiovascular risk, and blood is more informative the younger the person is.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: the younger you are, the more your blood tells me about your risk of cardiovascular disease.
verification_candidates.rationale: A quantified claim about the diagnostic value of blood tests for heart disease risk.

verification_candidates.claim_text: A coronary calcium score usually becomes less relevant as patients get older, though it can be somewhat helpful in younger patients.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: usually by the time they're older, a calcium score becomes less relevant. Calcium score can be somewhat helpful in a younger patient, though.
verification_candidates.rationale: A claim about the diagnostic usefulness of a common heart test by age.

verification_candidates.claim_text: In a study reported in an atherosclerosis journal, fifty percent of patients who had cardiac events had them at the site of non-calcified lesions, which undercuts the value of a low calcium score.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: looking at fifty percent of patients that had that had events had them at the site. Of non-calcified lesions
verification_candidates.rationale: A specific study finding that can be checked and affects trust in calcium scoring.

verification_candidates.claim_text: Blood tests give the least insight into cancer risk, and will until liquid biopsies are fully functioning.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: On the cancer side, I think that's really, frankly, where blood gives us the least insight.
verification_candidates.rationale: A claim about the current diagnostic value of blood testing for cancer.

verification_candidates.claim_text: GRAIL's liquid biopsy probably looks mostly at RNA and DNA.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: I think GRAIL is probably looking mostly at RNA and DNA.
verification_candidates.rationale: A checkable statement about how a commercial cancer test works.

verification_candidates.claim_text: Virtually every cancer is the result of a somatic mutation, not a germline mutation.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: virtually every cancer is a result of a somatic mutation, not a germline mutation.
verification_candidates.rationale: A sweeping causal claim about the origin of cancers that can be checked against cancer genetics.

verification_candidates.claim_text: Knowing your genotype does not help much in assessing cancer risk, outside a few outliers such as BRCA or Lynch.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: knowing your genotype doesn't really help, outside of a few outlier things like BRCA or Lynch.
verification_candidates.rationale: Bears on whether listeners pursue genetic testing for cancer risk.

verification_candidates.claim_text: Cancer risk comes down to inflammation and metabolic health.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: in cancer, it really comes down to understanding inflammation, which we've already addressed, and metabolic health
verification_candidates.rationale: A causal claim about cancer risk factors that steers prevention choices.
